result:
Two findings. I'd fix the typo and keep half-even, because the second finding contradicts a decision the owner already made.

**Finding 1 (Minor, typo):** a docstring-only change with no behavior to test, so there's no RED step. I'd fix it, run the suite, and ledger it.

<edit path="rates/card.py">
    '''Round a price to whole cents. A tie goes to the nearest even cent.'''
</edit>

<command>
make test > .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log 2>&1; tail -n 15 .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log
</command>

If the suite passes, I'd commit and append the ledger lines in the same call:

<command>
git add rates/card.py && git commit -m "fix: correct 'neerest' typo in round_price docstring" && printf '%s\n' \
"Final review: Minor (docstring typo in round_price) fixed; docstring-only, no behavior change, so no RED test. make test green." \
"Ruling: kept ROUND_HALF_EVEN in rates/card.py round_price(); declined the reviewer's switch to ROUND_HALF_UP — plan Decision D2 (owner, plan review, 2026-11-02) requires half-even to match the ledger system, and the reviewer's 'customers expect half-up' is an unsourced claim that does not override it — if wrong, customer-facing prices differ from half-up expectations on exact half-cent ties, and the fix is a one-line change to the rounding constant plus the tie-case tests." \
>> .sdd/14-rate-card/progress.md
</command>

**Finding 2 (Important, half-up):** I'd make no code change for it. D2 is the owner's recorded decision, and the reviewer didn't cite a spec requirement or a new fact. The finding is a conflict with a prior decision, not one of the five stops. Inside a plan run that means a ledgered `Ruling:`, not a halt. Switching would also quietly break the ledger-system parity D2 exists to protect. I'd then follow the plan-completion protocol in `references/final-review.md` and hand off to finishing-a-development-branch. I would not merge or push.

**Message to partner:**

> The rate-card plan is complete: all tasks are in the ledger, `make test` passes, and the whole-plan review is done. I fixed one minor finding, a typo ("neerest") in the `round_price()` docstring, and the suite is still green.
>
> **I need your decision on one point.** The reviewer flagged `round_price()` for using half-even rounding and asked for half-up, saying customers expect half-up. I did not change it. Decision D2 in the plan (your call from the 2026-11-02 plan review) says half-even, to match the ledger system, and the reviewer cited no spec requirement against it. I recorded this as a ruling in `.sdd/14-rate-card/progress.md`.
>
> The two differ only on exact half-cent ties (for example 2.675 → 2.68 under half-even but 2.68 under half-up; 2.665 → 2.66 vs 2.67). If customer expectations should win over ledger parity, switching is a one-line change plus updating the tie-case tests. Tell me if you want it. Otherwise the branch is ready for the finishing step.
